t: Elam joined lowland Susa and highland Anshan in southwestern Iran, a pairing that let it survive conquest and revive for two millennia.
It repeatedly broke Mesopotamian powers, sacking Ur and toppling Kassite Babylon, and its rulers once outranked Hammurabi.
Ashurbanipal destroyed Susa c. 646 BCE, but Elamite language and bureaucracy lived on inside the Persian Achaemenid state.
dyk: The Code of Hammurabi was found at Susa, not Babylon: Elamite kings carried it off as a war trophy c. 1158 BCE, and French excavators recovered it around 1900.
ev: Kutik-Inshushinak of Awan first unifies Susa and the highlands after the Akkadian collapse
Shimashki king Kindattu sacks Ur and captures Ibbi-Sin, last ruler of the Third Dynasty of Ur
Sukkalmah Siwe-Palar-Khuppak conquers Eshnunna and is addressed as 'father' by Hammurabi
Shutruk-Nahhunte and Kutir-Nahhunte overthrow the Kassite dynasty of Babylon
Humban-nikash I fights Sargon II of Assyria at the Battle of Der
Sennacherib's son Ashur-nadin-shumi is handed to Elam and dies in captivity
Ashurbanipal destroys Susa, looting its treasuries and desecrating royal tombs
Cyrus the Great begins absorbing Elam into the Achaemenid Empire
